met_analysis:
The well marked low pressure area over Jharkhand weakened into a low pressure area and lies over southeast Jharkhand & neighbourhood. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 4.5 km above mean sea level.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Firozpur, Karnal, Badaun, Prayagraj, centre of low pressure area over southeast Jharkhand & neighbourhood, Digha & thence southeastwards to Eastcentral Bay of Bengal.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northwest Bay of Bengal between 5.8 & 7.6 km above mean sea levels persists.
The Shear Zone roughly along Lat. 22°N across central & adjoining north Peninsular India persists and now seen between 5.8 & 7.6 km above mean sea levels.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhoodat 3.1 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over central Assam and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over Central Pakistan with a trough aloft in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 30°N has moved northeastwards.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northwest Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhoodat 0.9 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The north-south trough from northwest Rajasthan to northeast Arabian sea across Gujarat at 1.5 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
